slides.title: Six little stories
slides.transcript: [warmly] Yaseen’s Big Year. Six little stories, for Yaseen. <break time="0.5s" /> [gently] Preschool, soccer, trains by the sea — and a little sister on the way.

slides.title: Hello, Yaseen!
slides.transcript: [warmly] Hello, Yaseen! <break time="0.4s" /> This is Yaseen. He lives in San Diego, where the sky is blue, the sun is warm, and the tall palm trees wave hello. Yaseen is four years old. He has black hair, rosy cheeks, and the biggest smile you ever saw. <break time="0.5s" /> [softly] Hello, Yaseen!

slides.title: So Much Love
slides.transcript: [warmly] So Much Love. <break time="0.4s" /> Mama loves Yaseen so much. Baba loves Yaseen so much — and Baba has his own special name for him: Yasso! They love him when he is happy and when he is grumpy, when he is fast and when he is sleepy. Every single day, they wrap him up in the biggest, warmest hug, and Baba says, “Yasso, you’re gamed gedan!” — which means really, really awesome. <break time="0.5s" /> [softly] Yasso is gamed gedan!

slides.title: Yaseen’s Favourite Things
slides.transcript: [warmly] Yaseen’s Favourite Things. <break time="0.4s" /> Yaseen has favourite things. His black-and-white soccer ball. His trains — long ones, fast ones, and the red trolley that goes ding-ding. And books, lots of books, especially at bedtime. What are your favourite things? <break time="0.5s" /> [softly] Ball! Trains! Books!

slides.title: Good Morning
slides.transcript: [warmly] Good Morning. <break time="0.4s" /> The sun peeks through the window. Yaseen opens his eyes, stretches up high, and says, “Bismillah.” Down in the kitchen there is crunchy cereal and cold orange juice. Crunch, crunch, slurp! A big boy needs a big breakfast. <break time="0.5s" /> [softly] Bismillah!

slides.title: All By Myself
slides.transcript: [warmly] All By Myself. <break time="0.4s" /> Now it is time to get dressed. Arm in, arm in, head through — pop! Yaseen puts on his red t-shirt all by himself. Then his jeans. Then one sock… where is the other sock? There it is! “I did it all by myself!” <break time="0.5s" /> [softly] All by myself!

slides.title: A New Backpack
slides.transcript: [warmly] A New Backpack. <break time="0.4s" /> One night, Mama put a brand-new blue backpack on Yaseen’s bed. “Tomorrow you start preschool!” Yaseen hugged the backpack. It was exciting… and a tiny bit scary. “What if I don’t know anyone?” Mama kissed his head. “New things feel big at first. Then they feel just right.” <break time="0.5s" /> [softly] New things feel big at first.

slides.title: Ding-Ding!
slides.transcript: [warmly] Ding-Ding! <break time="0.4s" /> In the morning, Yaseen and Baba walked to preschool. And look — what was coming down the street? The big red trolley! Ding-ding! Yaseen counted the cars: one, two, three! “Bye, trolley!” The trolley was going to work, and Yaseen was going to preschool. <break time="0.5s" /> [softly] Ding-ding!

slides.title: A Wiggly Tummy
slides.transcript: [warmly] A Wiggly Tummy. <break time="0.4s" /> At the preschool door, Yaseen stopped. There were so many children, and so many new faces. His tummy felt wiggly, like jelly. He held Baba’s hand very, very tight. “It’s okay to feel wiggly, Yasso,” said Baba. “Brave doesn’t mean not scared. Brave means trying anyway.” <break time="0.5s" /> [softly] Brave means trying anyway.

slides.title: One Big Breath
slides.transcript: [warmly] One Big Breath. <break time="0.4s" /> Yaseen took one big breath in… and let it out slowly. Whoooosh. He gave Baba a hug. “I’ll come back to get you after lunch, Yasso,” said Baba. “Promise?” “Promise.” Then Yaseen walked in all by himself, and waved goodbye with a brave little smile. <break time="0.5s" /> [softly] Whoooosh!

slides.title: Circle Time
slides.transcript: [warmly] Circle Time. <break time="0.4s" /> Inside, everyone sat on a big rainbow carpet in a circle. They sang a good-morning song, and they clapped, and they counted to ten. Yaseen sang the loudest when they got to four — because four is how old he is! <break time="0.5s" /> [softly] One, two, three, FOUR!

slides.title: Paint and Play
slides.transcript: [warmly] Paint and Play. <break time="0.4s" /> Then it was time to make things. Yaseen painted a long, long train with red, blue and yellow cars. He got paint on his fingers, and a little bit on his nose! He built a tall tower with blocks, and it fell down — crash! — so he built it again. <break time="0.5s" /> [softly] Crash! Build it again!

slides.title: The People Train
slides.transcript: [warmly] The People Train. <break time="0.4s" /> Outside on the playground, Yaseen had an idea. “Let’s be a train!” One friend held his shoulders, then another, then another. Chugga-chugga, choo-choo! The people train went round the slide, under the climbing frame, and all the way back again. <break time="0.5s" /> [softly] Chugga-chugga, choo-choo!

slides.title: A New Friend
slides.transcript: [warmly] A New Friend. <break time="0.4s" /> Then Yaseen saw a boy sitting all alone. He looked wiggly inside, just like Yaseen had felt at the door. Yaseen remembered. He walked over and said, “Want to build a train with me?” The boy smiled a tiny smile. Together they built the longest train in the whole preschool. <break time="0.5s" /> [softly] Want to build with me?

slides.title: Soccer Day!
slides.transcript: [warmly] Soccer Day! <break time="0.4s" /> Saturday morning is soccer day! Yaseen puts on his blue jersey with the number 4, his white shorts, his stripy socks and his shin guards. Then his boots — tie, tie, tight! At the field, Coach blows the whistle. Tweeeet! “Let’s play!” <break time="0.5s" /> [softly] Tweeeet!

slides.title: Warm Up!
slides.transcript: [warmly] Warm Up! <break time="0.4s" /> First, everybody warms up. Reach up high to the sky! Touch your toes! Ten jumping jacks — jump, clap, jump, clap! Then a jog all the way around the field. “Warm muscles are happy muscles,” says Coach. Yaseen’s muscles are very happy. <break time="0.5s" /> [softly] Jump, clap! Jump, clap!

slides.title: Tap, Tap, Tap
slides.transcript: [warmly] Tap, Tap, Tap. <break time="0.4s" /> Now Coach puts out a line of little orange cones. Yaseen dribbles the ball in and out, in and out — tap, tap, tap with the inside of his foot, keeping the ball close, as if it were tied to his foot with a magic string. He goes all the way to the end and doesn’t knock over a single cone! <break time="0.5s" /> [softly] Tap, tap, tap!

slides.title: Big Ears
slides.transcript: [warmly] Big Ears. <break time="0.4s" /> Then Coach calls everyone over. Yaseen sits down on the grass. He listens with big ears and watching eyes. “Pass to your friends,” says Coach. “Soccer is a team game.” Good players listen first — and Yaseen is a very good listener. <break time="0.5s" /> [softly] Good players listen first.

slides.title: GOAL!
slides.transcript: [warmly] GOAL! <break time="0.4s" /> Game time! Yaseen passes the ball to his friend. His friend passes it back. Yaseen runs, looks up, and — kick! The ball flies into the net so hard it nearly tears it — ata3 el shabaka! GOAL! The whole team jumps and cheers. Coach gives Yaseen a high five. “Great pass, great goal, Yaseen!” And from the side of the field, Baba shouts, “Yasso is gamed gedan!” <break time="0.5s" /> [softly] Kick, kick… GOAL!

slides.title: Fall Down, Get Up
slides.transcript: [warmly] Fall Down, Get Up. <break time="0.4s" /> Sometimes Yaseen falls down. Bump! His knee gets grass on it, and it stings a little. But Yaseen gets right back up and keeps playing. At the end of the game, he shakes hands with the other team. “Good game!” Win or lose, that’s what a soccer star does. <break time="0.5s" /> [softly] Good game!

slides.title: Practice With Baba
slides.transcript: [warmly] Practice With Baba. <break time="0.4s" /> Why is Yaseen so good at soccer? Because he practises! In the evening, when the sky turns gold, he and Baba play in the backyard. Baba is the goalkeeper. Yaseen dribbles, aims, and — kick! Sometimes Baba catches it. Sometimes… GOAL! “Strong feet, Yasso,” says Baba, “and a strong heart. You’re gamed gedan!” <break time="0.5s" /> [softly] Strong feet, strong heart!

slides.title: Trip Day!
slides.transcript: [warmly] Trip Day! <break time="0.4s" /> One sunny Sunday, Baba said, “Yasso! Who wants to go to Del Mar to see the trains?” “ME!” shouted Yaseen. He put on his sun hat. He packed a snack box with crackers, grapes and a cheese sandwich. “Ready!” he said — before Baba had even found the car keys. <break time="0.5s" /> [softly] Who wants to see the trains? ME!

slides.title: Along the Coast
slides.transcript: [warmly] Along the Coast. <break time="0.4s" /> Yaseen buckled up in his car seat — click! They drove up along the coast. Out of the window he could see the blue ocean, the white waves, and surfers riding them. “Are we there yet?” “Almost.” “Are we there yet?” “Almost!” “ARE WE THERE YET?” “…Yes!” <break time="0.5s" /> [softly] Are we there yet?

slides.title: Up on the Cliffs
slides.transcript: [warmly] Up on the Cliffs. <break time="0.4s" /> At Del Mar, they walked along a path at the top of the cliffs. Far, far below was the sea. And down there, running right along the edge of the ocean, were the train tracks! “We stay behind the fence, Yasso,” said Baba, “far back from the tracks. Trains are big and fast.” Yaseen held Baba’s hand. “Far back,” he said. <break time="0.5s" /> [softly] We stay far back!

slides.title: Listen…
slides.transcript: [warmly] Listen… <break time="0.4s" /> They sat down to wait. Yaseen listened very carefully. He heard the seagulls: squawk, squawk! He heard the waves: shhh, shhh. Then… he heard something else. A rumble. A rumble that got bigger, and bigger, and BIGGER. Yaseen cupped his hand to his ear. “Baba! Is it coming?” <break time="0.5s" /> [softly] Rumble, rumble, RUMBLE…

slides.title: BEEP BEEP!
slides.transcript: [warmly] BEEP BEEP! <break time="0.4s" /> Here it comes! A long train came zooming along the edge of the sea, right below the cliffs. Yaseen jumped up and waved with both hands, as high as he could. And the train driver saw him, and the train went — BEEP! BEEP! Just for Yaseen! <break time="0.5s" /> [softly] BEEP! BEEP!

slides.title: Count the Cars
slides.transcript: [warmly] Count the Cars. <break time="0.4s" /> “Let’s count the cars!” said Yaseen. One, two, three, four, five! “Is it the Coaster or the Surfliner?” asked Baba. Yaseen looked carefully. “The Surfliner! It goes all the way to Los Angeles!” Then the train went round the bend and was gone. “Bye, train! Come back soon!” <break time="0.5s" /> [softly] One, two, three, four, five!

slides.title: Sunset Picnic
slides.transcript: [warmly] Sunset Picnic. <break time="0.4s" /> They spread out a blanket and ate their picnic. Crackers, crunch! Grapes, pop! The sun sank down into the sea, orange and pink and gold. Yaseen leaned on Baba. “Alhamdulillah for trains,” he said, “and for the sea, and for you, Baba.” <break time="0.5s" /> [softly] Alhamdulillah!

slides.title: The Big News
slides.transcript: [warmly] The Big News. <break time="0.4s" /> One evening, Mama and Baba sat with Yaseen on the sofa. Mama took his hand and put it gently on her round tummy. “Yaseen,” she said, “there is a baby growing in here. A little sister. And you are going to be her big brother.” Yaseen’s eyes went very wide. “A sister? For ME?” <break time="0.5s" /> [softly] A sister? For ME?

slides.title: Will You Still Love Me?
slides.transcript: [warmly] Will You Still Love Me? <break time="0.4s" /> Later, Yaseen got very quiet. He climbed into Mama’s lap. “When the baby comes,” he whispered, “will you still love me?” Mama and Baba hugged him tight, tight, tight. “Love doesn’t get smaller when a family gets bigger,” said Baba. “It gets BIGGER. We will always, always love you, Yasso.” <break time="0.5s" /> [softly] Love gets bigger!

slides.title: How Small?
slides.transcript: [warmly] How Small? <break time="0.4s" /> “How big will she be?” asked Yaseen. Baba picked up Yaseen’s soccer ball. “Her whole head will be smaller than this,” he said. Then Mama showed him a pair of baby socks. They were so tiny they fit on Yaseen’s thumbs! “She’ll be very small,” said Mama, “and very, very soft.” <break time="0.5s" /> [softly] So tiny!

slides.title: Kick!
slides.transcript: [warmly] Kick! <break time="0.4s" /> One night, Yaseen pressed his ear against Mama’s tummy to say goodnight to the baby. And then — bump! Something pushed against his cheek! “She kicked me!” laughed Yaseen. “She kicks like a soccer player! I’m going to teach her everything.” <break time="0.5s" /> [softly] Bump! She kicked!

slides.title: Gentle Hands
slides.transcript: [warmly] Gentle Hands. <break time="0.4s" /> Baba sat down with Yaseen. “Your feet are strong, Yasso,” he said. “Strong feet are for kicking the ball. But babies need something different. Babies need gentle hands.” Yaseen looked at his hands. He made them soft, like a feather. “Soft hands,” said Yaseen. “Slow hands. Gentle hands.” <break time="0.5s" /> [softly] Soft hands, slow hands, gentle hands.

slides.title: Practice
slides.transcript: [warmly] Practice. <break time="0.4s" /> Yaseen knows that to get good at something, you practise — just like soccer. So he practised with Teddy. He wrapped Teddy in a blanket. He held Teddy’s head in the crook of his arm. He rocked him slowly, slowly, and whispered, “Shh, shh, it’s okay.” “Great practice,” said Mama. <break time="0.5s" /> [softly] Shh, shh, it’s okay.

slides.title: Her Room
slides.transcript: [warmly] Her Room. <break time="0.4s" /> Then it was time to get the baby’s room ready. Baba built the crib. Mama hung up soft pink curtains. And Yaseen had the most important job: folding the tiny baby clothes. A tiny shirt. Tiny trousers. Tiny, tiny socks. “Everything is so small!” he said. <break time="0.5s" /> [softly] Tiny, tiny, tiny!

slides.title: A Present for Her
slides.transcript: [warmly] A Present for Her. <break time="0.4s" /> “Can I give her a present?” asked Yaseen. He thought and thought. A soccer ball? Too big. A storybook? Not yet. Then he knew! He picked a soft, squishy, blue toy train and put it in her crib. “Choo-choo,” he whispered. “This is from your big brother.” <break time="0.5s" /> [softly] From your big brother.

slides.title: It’s Time!
slides.transcript: [warmly] It’s Time! <break time="0.4s" /> Very early one morning, while it was still a little bit dark, Baba woke Yaseen up. “It’s time!” he said. “The baby is coming today!” Mama and Baba went to the hospital, and Yaseen stayed with someone who loves him — and waited, and waited, and waited. <break time="0.5s" /> [softly] It’s time!

slides.title: A Picture for Her
slides.transcript: [warmly] A Picture for Her. <break time="0.4s" /> While he waited, Yaseen drew a picture for his sister. He drew a big red trolley and a long train by the sea. He drew a soccer ball. And he drew himself, holding a tiny baby with very gentle hands. “This is you,” he said, “and this is me. Your big brother.” <break time="0.5s" /> [softly] This is me. Your big brother.

slides.title: She’s Here!
slides.transcript: [warmly] She’s Here! <break time="0.4s" /> And then, at last, Yaseen met her. His little sister. She was so tiny. Her nose was tiny, her ears were tiny, and her fingers were the tiniest of all. Yaseen held out one finger, very gently — and she wrapped her whole hand around it and held on tight. “Hello, little sister,” said Yaseen. “I’m Yaseen.” <break time="0.5s" /> [softly] Hello, little sister.

slides.title: Holding Her
slides.transcript: [warmly] Holding Her. <break time="0.4s" /> “Would you like to hold her?” asked Mama. Yaseen sat right back on the sofa with a big cushion under his arm. Baba laid the baby in his arms and kept a hand close by. Yaseen remembered his practice with Teddy. Head in the crook of his arm. Soft hands, slow hands, gentle hands. She yawned a tiny yawn. “I’m doing it,” whispered Yaseen. Baba smiled. “Yasso, you’re gamed gedan.” <break time="0.5s" /> [softly] Soft hands, slow hands, gentle hands.

slides.title: Big Brother Jobs
slides.transcript: [warmly] Big Brother Jobs. <break time="0.4s" /> Being a big brother is an important job. Yaseen fetches a clean nappy when Mama needs one. He brings the soft blanket. He sings to the baby while she has her milk. And he shows her his soccer ball — but he never, ever kicks it near her. “Ball games are for outside,” says Yaseen. “Babies are for gentle.” <break time="0.5s" /> [softly] What a helper!

slides.title: Yaseen Time
slides.transcript: [warmly] Yaseen Time. <break time="0.4s" /> Babies need lots and lots of looking after. But every single night, there is still Yaseen time. A story with Mama. A tickle and a game with Baba. “You were our very first baby,” says Mama, “and you will always be our Yaseen. Our love just grew bigger — big enough for two.” <break time="0.5s" /> [softly] Big enough for two!

slides.title: The Whisper Voice
slides.transcript: [warmly] The Whisper Voice. <break time="0.4s" /> One afternoon the baby started to cry. Waaah! Waaah! Yaseen didn’t shout, and he didn’t cover his ears. He tiptoed to her crib. He used his softest whisper voice, and he sang the choo-choo song, slow and quiet: “Choo… choo… little train… time to sleep…” And slowly, slowly, she stopped crying and closed her eyes. <break time="0.5s" /> [softly] Shhh… choo… choo…

slides.title: Promises
slides.transcript: [warmly] Promises. <break time="0.4s" /> Yaseen lay down next to his sister on her play mat. “When you’re bigger,” he told her, “I’m going to teach you to dribble — tap, tap, tap. I’ll show you the paints at preschool. And Baba and I will take you to Del Mar, and we’ll stand far back behind the fence, and the train will go BEEP BEEP — just for you.” <break time="0.5s" /> [softly] Just for you!

slides.title: Goodnight, Yaseen
slides.transcript: [softly] Goodnight, Yaseen. <break time="0.4s" /> The moon is up over the ocean. The trains are sleeping. The soccer ball is resting on the shelf. Mama and Baba tuck Yaseen in and kiss him goodnight. “Goodnight, Yasso,” whispers Baba. “You’re gamed gedan.” Strong feet for soccer. Happy waves for trains. Gentle hands for his little sister. And a family full of love. Goodnight, Yaseen. Goodnight, little sister. <break time="0.5s" /> [whispers] Goodnight, Yaseen.
